subject: Increasing Axis Spacing to Remove Overlaps

messages.author: 410e477af3aeaf0d
messages.subject: Increasing Axis Spacing to Remove Overlaps
parts:
Hi,

I'm using ggplot2 to make a chart which displays information about
some factored data. The problem I've got is that the values tend to
overlap and obscure each other. The points, their size and amount of
fill convey the information so it's important that a) they are large
enough to be clearly visible and b) they don't overlap each other. Is
there a way to space out the axes (primarily just the y axis) further?
Ideally the spacing would be related to my own sizing variable:
base.size

Here's the code needed to replicate my .

library(ggplot2)
answer.scheme <- data.frame(n = factor(1:30), c = factor(rep(1:2,
each=30)), correct = sample(c(TRUE,FALSE), 60, replace = TRUE))
detection.results <- data.frame(n = factor(1:30), c = factor(rep(1:2,
each=30)), Freq = sample(0:120, 60, replace = TRUE))
X <- merge(answer.scheme, detection.results, by = c("c","n"))
base.size <- 10
scaleSize <- function(x){ base.size * (1 - ( x / 120)) }
plot <- ggplot(data = subset(X, correct == TRUE), aes(c, n))
plot <- plot + geom_point(colour = "forestgreen", size = base.size)
plot <- plot + geom_point(data = subset(X, correct == TRUE & Freq > 0
& Freq < max(Freq)), aes(size = scaleSize(Freq)), colour = "white")
plot <- plot + geom_point(data = subset(X, correct == FALSE & Freq >
0), shape = 17, aes(size = scaleSize(Freq)), colour = "red2")
plot + theme_bw() + opts(legend.position = "none")

Any pointers would be most appreciated.
Thanks,
Alastair

messages.subject: Re: Increasing Axis Spacing to Remove Overlaps
parts:
This is probably a funky workaround, but I'm pretty proud of the result. 

If you set the dimensions of a ggsave()... say:

ggsave("test.png", height=10, width=2)

It looks like the attached file. Not a bad result. Is that what you're looking for?

Brandon

messages.subject: Re: Increasing Axis Spacing to Remove Overlaps
parts:
Can't get it exactly, but maybe the answer lies in converting n to a continuous variable (X$ncont <- as.numberic(X$n) * 3) then you'll get separation of (e.g.) 3. Of course you'll need to supply n as breaks and labels for the y axis. I suppose you'll need to ensure coordination between the separation of the lines and the size of the shapes (maybe times by base.size?)

That should work at any size of the picture, I'm sure you can control the output dimensions in Sweave.
